name: Repair electronics
summary: Most dead electronics fail in a few places: bulging or leaking capacitors, blown fuses, cracked solder joints and broken connectors. Find the fault with your eyes and a multimeter, then take the replacement from a donor board. The same parts sit in thousands of chargers, TVs and power supplies.

parts.why: The most common failure: bulging, leaking or dried out
Blown fuses are cheap, quick fixes
Shorted rectifier diodes in power supplies
Switching transistors that fail in power supplies
Regulators that feed the rest of the board

tips: Look first. Bulging capacitors, burnt spots and cracked joints often show the fault.
Discharge big capacitors before touching any mains power board.
Replace a capacitor with the same capacity and the same or higher voltage rating.
A fuse that blows again at once means a short somewhere. Find it. Never fit a bigger fuse.
